principles: One causal-evidence boundary owns execution-key derivation, CAS receipt persistence, selector-specific fan-out, and metrics.
Reuse is admissible only for an exact execution-key match with a valid immutable receipt; legacy evidence without the new identity remains strict and non-reusable.
Freshness invalidation is dependency-domain based but never weaker than current materialHash/DONE-required policy.
Preflight is fail-closed and runs before any expensive child process.
drivers: Reduce repeated command cost in multi-intent verification while preserving each selector verdict.
Survive canonical metadata/Git commit failure without losing a completed command receipt or re-running it.
Avoid false-fresh evidence after related story-owned changes and avoid unrelated specialized reruns.
Make savings and correctness visible in structured and operator-facing output.

options.name: Shared causal-evidence service
pros: One implementation can serve single and batch evidence paths, stale refresh, and certification consumers.
Keeps receipt/key/metric semantics out of individual handlers.
cons: Requires explicit compatibility adapters for existing VerificationExecutionReceipt and legacy evidence.

options.name: Patch each handler independently
pros: Smaller first diff in each file.
cons: Duplicates identity and retry rules and makes divergence likely across add, batch, refresh, and validation.

options.name: Relax existing freshness globally
cons: Violates the strict DONE-required policy and can admit false-fresh evidence.

rationale: A shared core service is the only option that can enforce one exact execution identity and one receipt-first transaction across single/batch execution while preserving selector-specific verdicts and existing strict gates. Existing handlers become thin adapters; global freshness relaxation is explicitly rejected.

preMortem.scenario: Two intents with the same command but different selectors incorrectly share a PASS.
preMortem.trigger: Fan-out copies receipt success without evaluating the receiving intent selector.
preMortem.consequence: A selector-specific verification gap becomes covered evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Store captured output digest/tail in the receipt and evaluate every intent selector independently before writing its evidence row; test a mismatching fan-out selector.

preMortem.scenario: Canonical checklist import fails after a command has completed.
preMortem.trigger: Import/commit is coupled to execution or receipt persistence overwrites the existing receipt.
preMortem.consequence: A retry reruns an expensive command or produces a new receipt hash.
preMortem.mitigation: Persist and verify the immutable receipt first, then retry only an idempotent canonical import transaction keyed by the same execution key and receipt hash.

preMortem.scenario: An unrelated main merge invalidates or reruns specialized evidence incorrectly.
preMortem.trigger: Dependency domains are inferred from a coarse whole-tree hash or a missing domain declaration is treated as fresh.
preMortem.consequence: Either wasted reruns or false-fresh evidence after related changes.
preMortem.mitigation: Shadow-compare declarative domains, keep strict materialHash fallback, and have CertificationWindow consume only explicit affected-node decisions.

preMortem.scenario: Preflight reports readiness after a writer/index/evidence target check races or is not performed.
preMortem.trigger: Preflight is implemented as advisory logging after children start.
preMortem.consequence: A long run cannot persist its result and leaves partial evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Run all preflight checks before scheduling children and record zero command executions on failure.
